Collaborator

Closes [#159](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/159)

Why
---

Issue [#159](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/159) (child of [#149](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/149), depends on [#157](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/157)). [#157](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/157) added multiple pages to a drawing, but there was no way to remove the elements on a page except deleting them by hand. Excalidraw's existing "Clear canvas" option also didn't know about pages. This issue adds a **clearing mode** to the Pages sidebar: you select one, several or all pages and clear them after a confirmation, and the pages themselves are kept. It also changes "Clear canvas" so that, with more than one page, you can clear just the page you're on (the canvas) or that page and every other page (its sub-canvases).

How this PR answers the issue's open questions:

*   **How are selected pages shown?** Each page gets a checkbox with a check mark and a red border when selected.
*   **Can you navigate between pages in clearing mode?** No. Clicking a page selects or deselects it. Exit clearing mode to navigate.
*   **Is there an extra indicator for clearing mode?** Yes, a red "Clearing mode: select pages to clear" header above the page list.

While testing with many pages, the page list turned out not to scroll: pages past the bottom of the window were cut off. This PR fixes that too.

What changed
------------

*   **Clearing-mode state (`types.ts`, `appState.ts`):** a new `AppState.pageClearingSelection: readonly string[] | null`. `null` means clearing mode is off; otherwise it holds the ids of the selected pages. It lives in each editor's own state, so two drawings on one page don't affect each other. It is never saved to local storage, exports or the server.
*   **Clearing pages (`App.tsx`):**
    *   New public methods `getPageIds()`, `getActivePageId()` and `clearPages(pageIds)`, also added to `AppClassProperties`.
    *   `clearPages` empties pages that aren't open by setting their stored `elements` to `[]`. For the page you're on, it marks its elements deleted through `updateScene`, so that clear can be undone, and resets the selection.
    *   Pages keep their settings (background, scroll, grid). Image files aren't removed, because other pages may still use them.
    *   Private handlers for entering and exiting clearing mode, toggling a page, selecting or deselecting all, and clearing the selection. After a clear, clearing mode stays on and the selection resets.
*   **Clearing-mode UI (`Pages.tsx`, `Pages.scss`, `LayerUI.tsx`):**
    *   Normal mode: an **Enter clearing mode** button under **\+ Add page**. Both are disabled in view mode.
    *   Clearing mode:
        *   Each page becomes a checkbox (`role="checkbox"`, `aria-checked`). The page you're on gets a "Current" badge and `aria-current="page"`.
        *   Buttons: **Select all pages / Deselect all pages**, **Clear** (disabled until something is selected), and **Exit clearing mode**. **Add page** is hidden.
        *   **Clear** opens a confirmation stating how many pages will be cleared. Its state is local to the component, so it's per editor, and it's dropped whenever clearing mode turns on or off.
*   **Seeing the page while clearing (`DefaultSidebar.tsx`):** while clearing mode is on and the Pages tab is open, the sidebar is forced to dock, the same way the search tab already is. The canvas shrinks beside the menu instead of being covered, and clicking the canvas doesn't close the menu. Closing the sidebar doesn't end clearing mode; reopening it shows clearing mode again.
*   **Clear canvas (`actionCanvas.tsx`, `ActiveConfirmDialog.tsx`, `ConfirmDialog.tsx`):**
    *   `actionClearCanvas` takes `{ scope?: "canvas" | "allPages" }`. With `"allPages"`, it calls `clearPages` on every other page, then clears the current page as before. It also no longer exits clearing mode.
    *   With more than one page, the dialog (main menu, Ctrl+Delete, command palette) offers **Clear this canvas only** and **Clear canvas and all pages**. With one page it's unchanged.
    *   `ConfirmDialog` takes an optional second confirm button (`onSecondaryConfirm`, `secondaryConfirmText`). The shared close-and-refocus logic moved into a `runAndRefocus` helper.
*   **Scrollable page list (`Pages.scss`, `LayerUI.tsx`):** the page list now scrolls inside the sidebar, and the buttons stay pinned below it. The sidebar's flex layout had no `min-height: 0`, so the list grew past the window and the sidebar clipped it. The fix is scoped to the Pages tab (`.page-navigation-tab` and a `:has()` rule on the tabs root), so Library and Search are unchanged.
*   **Strings (`en.json`):** `labels.currentPage`, `labels.clearingMode`; `buttons.enterClearingMode`, `exitClearingMode`, `clearPages`, `selectAllPages`, `deselectAllPages`, `clearCanvasOnly`, `clearCanvasAndPages`; `clearCanvasDialog.withPages`; `clearPagesDialog.title`, `clearPagesDialog.content`.
*   **Snapshots:** four snapshot files gain `"pageClearingSelection": null` and nothing else.
*   **Mutation testing (sprint 3):**
    *   StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner, run with `yarn test:mutation` (`stryker.config.mjs`, `vitest.stryker.config.mts`).
    *   Reports and the write-up are in `docs/sprint3/mutation/`. The score went from 69.67% to 90.40%; details under Test Evidence.

Tech Debt
---------

### Introduced

*   **Only the current page's clear can be undone.** Undo history only tracks the open page, so pages that weren't open when you cleared them can't be restored. Undo/redo was out of scope for this issue.
*   **No navigation in clearing mode:** clicking a page selects it instead of opening it. You have to exit clearing mode to switch pages.
*   **The docked sidebar can't be undocked during clearing mode.** On narrow screens the docked sidebar takes a big share of the width.
*   **New strings are in `en.json` only.**
*   **`clearPages`, `getPageIds` and `getActivePageId` are public on `App`** but not part of `excalidrawAPI`, so host apps can't clear pages programmatically yet.

### Encountered

*   **The confirm dialog's state is shared between editors.** `activeConfirmDialogAtom` lives in `editorJotaiStore`, which is created once per module, so every editor on the page shares it: Ctrl+Delete in one drawing opens the Clear canvas dialog in all of them. Clearing mode avoids this by keeping its state in `AppState` and component state. The page tests reset the atom in `beforeEach`, because a dialog left open by one test otherwise leaked into the next.
*   **Pages are still in memory only (from [Implement Page Creation and Navigation #157](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/157)):** they aren't saved, exported or synced to collaborators, so cleared or uncleared pages other than the current one are lost on reload.
*   **The default sidebar's flex layout can't scroll long content:** no `min-height: 0` anywhere in the chain. This PR only fixes it for the Pages tab.
*   **Excalidraw's undo can't restore elements that were added outside history** (for example via `updateScene` without `CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY`). One test had to add its element in its own history step.
*   **Test failures not caused by this PR:**
    *   `scene/__snapshots__/export.test.ts.snap` has 1 obsolete snapshot from an earlier pages commit. It was left alone.

Test Evidence
-------------

All tests are in `packages/excalidraw/tests/pages.test.tsx` unless noted.

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |

| Clearing mode | "clearing mode" > "only shows clearing options while in clearing mode", "docks the pages sidebar while in clearing mode"; "clearing mode details" > "indicates the current page and the selected pages only while clearing" | integration | AC; docking is my reading of "open a menu to the side so that the user can still see the page" |
| Clear selection | "clearing mode" > "selects pages, confirms, and clears only the selected pages", "selects all pages and clears them, including the current one"; "clearing mode details" > "indicates the current page and the selected pages only while clearing" | integration | AC; issue open question (checkboxes) |
| Clearing confirmation | "clearing mode" > "selects pages, confirms, and clears only the selected pages" (Cancel clears nothing, Confirm clears); "clearing mode details" > "shows how many pages will be cleared and closes after confirming", "clears only the current page when it is the only one selected", "refreshes the previews of cleared pages that aren't open", "drops a pending confirmation when clearing mode is closed" | integration | AC; issue user scenario (clearing the current page); deselecting cleared elements is an implementation decision |
| Closing clearing mode | "clearing mode" > "only shows clearing options while in clearing mode" (stays on after closing and reopening the sidebar; Exit hides every clearing control), "selects pages, confirms, and clears only the selected pages" (still in clearing mode after a clear) | integration | AC |
| Clearing mode across page groups | "clearing mode" > "is scoped to a single drawing" (two `<Excalidraw>` editors: entering and exiting in one doesn't affect the other); "clearing mode details" > "never stores clearing mode with the drawing" | integration, unit | AC; not saving clearing mode is an implementation decision |
| Clear canvas option | "clear canvas" > "can clear only the current page", "can clear the current page and all other pages" (other pages are kept, but empty), "keeps the single confirm option when there is only one page"; "clear canvas dialog" > "closes after clearing only the current page", "clears the current page and all other pages in one undo step", "keeps everything when cancelled"; existing `shortcuts.test.tsx` > "Clear canvas shortcut should display confirm dialog" | integration | AC; clarified with the issue author: the canvas is the current page, the sub-canvases are the other pages, and clearing all keeps the empty pages |
| Beyond the ACs: sidebar docking rules | "sidebar docking" > "doesn't dock the pages sidebar outside clearing mode", "doesn't dock other sidebar tabs during clearing mode", "still docks the search sidebar" | integration | implementation decision; upstream behavior (search tab) |

**Not tested automatically, and why:**

*   **Scrolling the page list:** jsdom doesn't compute layout. It was checked once with a throwaway script (not committed) that opened the app in headless Edge and added 10 pages:
    *   The list scrolled (scrollHeight 1,492 px in a 524 px list).
    *   Page 10 was reachable by scrolling and by the mouse wheel.
    *   The buttons stayed pinned at the bottom, in normal and in clearing mode.
*   **Visual styling** of the check mark, the "Current" badge and the red header is only checked through class names and text, not visually.
*   **Phone layout** of the docked sidebar in clearing mode wasn't checked.
*   **Collaboration:** clearing pages in a collaboration room wasn't tested. Pages aren't synced yet (see Encountered).

AI-written tests

All tests added in this PR were written by AI (Claude Code). The existing test "creates pages and restores their elements, settings, and viewport" (from [#157](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/157)) was not changed. Its file got new imports, shared helpers and a `beforeEach` reset.

**`packages/excalidraw/tests/pages.test.tsx`** (modified)

*   "clearing mode" (5), "clear canvas" (3), "clearing mode details" (6), "sidebar docking" (3), "clear canvas dialog" (3).
*   The undo test was corrected once. It first expected one undo to bring back an element that the test helper had added outside undo history. Excalidraw can't restore such elements, so the test now adds an element in its own history step and expects only that one back.

**How expected values were checked:**

1.  Expected values come from the acceptance criteria, the issue's user scenario and open questions, and the author's clarifications ("canvas" is the current page; clearing all keeps the pages). Where the criteria are silent, they follow implementation decisions named in the table: docking, deselecting cleared elements, never saving clearing mode.
    
2.  **Mutation testing as the feature-disabled check:** StrykerJS mutated only the lines changed for [Implement Page Clearing #159](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/159) (`docs/sprint3/mutation/159-NotaThomas.md`).
    
    | Run | Mutants | Killed | Survived | No coverage | Score |
    
    | Before the second batch of tests | 211 | 147 | 62 | 2 | 69.67% |
    | After | 198 | 179 | 17 | 2 | 90.40% |
    
    *   Of the 19 mutants left, 16 are equivalent (unreachable guards, an analytics label, an unused class name, …) and 3 are minor test gaps, each explained in the write-up.
    *   Four pieces of code whose mutants couldn't change behavior were removed.
3.  Tests that failed for real reasons:
    
    *   Several new tests failed because a Clear canvas dialog left open by an earlier test leaked through the shared jotai store. This exposed the cross-editor dialog problem under Encountered.
    *   The undo test above failed because its expectation was wrong, not the code.

``[chore: move Stryker out of root deps to unblock Node 20 CI](/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/pull/181/commits/1dcf3c4694570e5d727e74ee3daaa4d87c7763b5 "chore: move Stryker out of root deps to unblock Node 20 CI Stryker's transitive @inquirer/* deps now require Node >=22.22, so the root `yarn install` failed on the Node 20 Lint and coverage runners even with Stryker pinned to 9.6.1. Stryker now lives in tools/mutation (outside the Yarn workspaces), which CI never installs. `yarn test:mutation` installs it on demand; Node's module resolution still finds the repo's vitest and typescript. `[1dcf3c4](/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/pull/181/commits/1dcf3c4694570e5d727e74ee3daaa4d87c7763b5)`

Stryker's transitive @inquirer/\* deps now require Node >=22.22, so the
root \`yarn install\` failed on the Node 20 Lint and coverage runners even
with Stryker pinned to 9.6.1.

Stryker now lives in tools/mutation (outside the Yarn workspaces), which
CI never installs. \`yarn test:mutation\` installs it on demand; Node's
module resolution still finds the repo's vitest and typescript. The root
yarn.lock is back to matching master.

Description
-----------

[![@AntWill-08](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/321958197?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/AntWill-08)

[AntWill-08](https://github.com/AntWill-08)

opened [on Nov 12, 2026](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/159#issue-6358679122)

Issue body actions

Issue Description
=================

Summary
-------

Allow users to remove elements from individual pages, multiple selected pages, or all pages without deleting the pages themselves.

User Story
----------

**As a** user, **I want** to be able to clear pages **so that** I can get rid of mistakes that I make and remove elements that I no longer want.

User Scenario
-------------

Developer adds the wrong diagram to one of their pages. The developer selected 'clear', which puts them in clearing mode, then selects 'clear current page', which deletes all elements on the current page. The developer then selects 'cancel' which returns them to normal mode.

* * *

Issue Classification
====================

Scope
-----

**Generic:** Medium  
**Specific:** Lesser medium (5 points)  
**Reason:** Clearing mode where user can select the individual pages they want to clear or mass select all pages to clear them all. Changing currently existing clear canvas functionality to work within the paradigm that the pages are sub-canvases of the main canvas. Changes to UI and underlying functionality.

* * *

Expectations
============

Acceptance Criteria
-------------------

*    **Clearing mode:** There should be a button that says 'enter clearing mode' around/in the navigation menu. When it is pressed, it should open a menu to the side so that the user can still see the page they are on. The menu should have an augmented navigation menu that displays all the pages and indicates in some way the page the user is currently on. There should be a 'clear' option and an option to exit clearing mode.
*    **Clear selection:** The user should be able to select the pages they want to clear from the augmented menu. The user should also be able to choose to select all pages. The pages they have selected should indicate that they have been selected.
*    **Clearing confirmation:** When the user selects the 'clear' option while in clearing mode, the user should be prompted to confirm their choice. If the user confirms it, then pages that were selected from the augmented menu should be cleared.
*    **Closing clearing mode:** The clearing options should only be visible when in clearing mode. Clearing mode should remain open until the user selects the exit option, which closes clearing mode.
*    **Clearing mode across page groups:** If there are two drawings that have pages, entering clearing mode in one should not enter clearing mode in the other, and exiting clearing mode in one should not exit clearing mode in the other.
*    **Clear canvas option:** There is already a clear canvas option that exists in Excalidraw. We are considering the pages to be 'sub-canvases', so the pre-existing clear canvas option should be changed to give the user the option to clear the canvas and all sub-canvases, or just the canvas.

Open Question
-------------

*   How should the pages selected to be cleared be indicated to the user? For example, should there be a checked box next to the selected pages?
*   Should the user should still be able to navigate to different pages while in clearing mode?
*   Should there be anything additional to indicated to the user that they are in clearing mode? For example, a banner telling the user that they are currently in clearing mode?

* * *

Extra
=====

Out of Scope
------------

*   Deleting pages
*   Changing anything about the properties of pages themselves that are unrelated to the elements on the page (the page order, page names, etc.)
*   Undo/redo functionality
*   Creating pages
*   Transferring elements from one page to another (ex. copying and pasting elements between pages)

    const page = this.pages.find((candidate) => candidate.id === pageId);
    if (!page) {
      throw new Error(`Cannot select unknown page ${pageId}`);
    }
    if (pageId === this.activePageId) {
      return;
    }

    this.saveActivePage();
    this.activePageId = pageId;
    this.history.clear();
    this.updateScene({
      elements: page.elements,
      appState: getPageActivationAppState(page.settings),
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });
  };

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 17:27:26Z)**_

I checked out PR #181's branch (`feat/issue-159-page-clearing`, Thomas Reilly / NotaThomas). It closes issue #159 and is ready for your manual testing.

**Links**
- PR: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/pull/181
- Issue: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/excalidraw/issues/159
- AI log for the branch: [2026-11-19_claude-code_issue-159-page-clearing.md](ai-logs/sprint3/NotaThomas/2026-11-19_claude-code_issue-159-page-clearing.md), plus [the failing-checks log](ai-logs/sprint3/NotaThomas/2026-11-19_claude-code_issue-159-PR-failing-checks-in-repo.md)
- Mutation write-up: [docs/sprint3/mutation/159-NotaThomas.md](docs/sprint3/mutation/159-NotaThomas.md)

**What I ran locally**
- I ran `pages.test.tsx`, `DefaultSidebar.test.tsx` and the four test files whose snapshots the PR changed (contextmenu, history, regressionTests, export). 174 tests passed and 1 was skipped.
- The typecheck (`tsc`) passes with no errors.
- The snapshot changes only add the new `pageClearingSelection: null` field.

**Code findings**
1. **It works as the issue asks.** Each of the 6 acceptance criteria has at least one test. The clearing-mode state is kept per editor and is never saved with the drawing. That covers the criterion that clearing mode in one drawing doesn't affect another.
2. **Clearing other pages with `elements: []` is safe today.** Pages only live in memory: they aren't saved and aren't shared in collaboration. If pages ever get saved or synced, this would need to mark the elements as deleted instead.
3. **Undo only partly works.** After "Clear canvas and all pages", one undo brings back the current page, but the other pages stay empty. The code comment says so, and the issue puts undo out of scope. Still, the test name "clears the current page and all other pages in one undo step" claims more than the test checks.
4. **Small inconsistency:** "Clear canvas and all pages" resets the current page's settings, such as background color, but leaves the other pages' settings alone.
5. **The PR is large because of generated files.** It shows about +25.7k lines, mostly mutation report JSON and `tools/mutation/yarn.lock`. The real source change is about 1.1k lines, most of it tests. The Stryker setup sits outside the main dependencies so CI doesn't install it, which is fine, but the reports make the PR heavy.
6. **It will conflict with your #158 branch.** Your commit `45599673` copied the range delete and scrollable list from this PR, so `Pages.tsx` and `Pages.scss` will clash depending on which merges first. Page deletion and clearing do work together: ids of deleted pages are ignored when clearing.
7. **AI disclosure:** the PR says Claude wrote all the tests. Several expected values are hand-picked element ids, which is fine. I didn't find any note in the log about the author checking the results by hand.

**Manual test checklist (`yarn start`)**
- [ ] With 2 or more pages, open the Pages sidebar and click "Enter clearing mode". The sidebar should dock, show a header, mark the current page with a badge, and show checkboxes.
- [ ] Clicking a page selects it and does not switch to it. "Select all" and "Deselect all" switch label correctly.
- [ ] "Clear" is greyed out until a page is selected. The confirmation shows the right count, and Cancel keeps everything.
